newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS BROUGHT DOWN TO EARTH BY UDINESE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS BROUGHT DOWN TO EARTH BY UDINESE.

text.p: Juventus, fresh from successive victories over former European Cup holders Milan and Ajax, were brought back to earth on Sunday with an astonishing 3-0 upset at home to 10-man Udinese.
Defeat left Parma, 1-0 winners at Roma, breathing down Juve's neck -- just three-points behind with seven matches of the season still to play.
Fifth-placed Inter can go third if they add to Milan's recent misery with a victory in the late night derby.
It was Juventus's third league defeat of the season and their first in 16 league and cup outings.
It was also their second successive home defeat to Udinese and their first in Turin since losing to Sampdoria by the same score exactly a year ago.
"We paid the price for a special week with two very special matches," said coach Marcello Lippi. "We had nothing left."
After last Sunday's historic 6-1 destruction of Milan and their midweek 2-1 victory in Amsterdam, Lippi had rested international midfielders Didier Deschamps and Angelo Di Livio.
The decision looked to have been vindicated when Regis Genaux, Udinese's Belgian defender, was sent off in the third minute for dissent.
But Udinese manager Alberto Zaccheroni bravely turned the match by persisting with three defenders and keeping Brazilian Marcio Amoroso and Germany's Oliver Bierhoff up front.
The move confused Juve who rarely looked like scoring and fell apart in 10 minutes either side of halftime.
First, Amoroso sent Peruzzi the wrong way with a 43rd minute penalty awarded for a foul on Bierhoff.

A minute after the interval, the German striker outjumped Ciro Ferrara to head his side's second, and, with Juve still recovering from that shock, Amoroso dribbled through their defence to add a third.
The European champions spurned two golden opportunities to get back into the match.
First, Christian Vieri blasted a penalty against the crossbar. Then, when the referee blew for a handball in the Udinese area, France's Zinedine Zidane saw his spotkick saved by Luigi Turci.
In the 59th minute, Juve's hopes of a comeback disappeared when midfielder Alessio Tacchinardi was dismissed for his second bookable offence.
The only bright note on Juve's dark day was the return of team captain Antonio Conte as a second-half substitute, out for six months after a knee operation.
But even that was clouded by news that their nearest rivals Parma had taken full advantage with victory at Roma, courtesy of a 43rd minute goal from Argentine Hernan Crespo.
Crespo's seventh goal of the season - and fourth in three matches - spoilt Nils Liedholm's return to football management at the age of 74 -- a record for Serie A.
Nicknamed "The Baron", Liedholm, who coached Roma to a league title in the 1980s, was brought in to replace Argentine Carlos Bianchi, sacked last week.

Roma fans, unhappy with their side's irratic form, went on strike for most of the match, filling the Olympic stadium with the sound of silence as Parma, coached by former Roma great Carlo Ancelotti, made all the running.

Sampdoria moved into third place after Vincenzo Montella's 18th goal of the season - from the penalty spot - accounted for Lazio, the club Samp's manager Sven-Goran Eriksson is widely expected to join at the end of the season.

Thanks in part to Montella's goals, the Genoa side enjoy a better goal difference than Bologna, who fought back from Stefano Torrisi's own-goal at Atalanta to force a 1-1 draw with Cristiano Scapolo's equaliser.
